data.name: Parvatam
data.gender_notes: Parvatam is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Parvatam is a name of the Hindu goddess Parvati, the consort of Lord Shiva. She is the embodiment of love, fertility, and nurturing. In mythology, Parvati is born from a mountain and marries Lord Shiva, who represents destruction and transformation. The name Parvatam carries the meaning “Mountain Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Parvatam usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Parvatam belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mountain Goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Parvatam total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.spiritual_significance: Parvatam, as the name of Parvati, represents the dormant divine feminine energy and the intense power of creation and nurturing that exists within all of us. It serves as a reminder of the innate potentials and strengths that lie within us, and how, like Parvati, we can use these energies to create loving relationships and a fulfilling life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Parvatam is a Sanskrit name meaning 'mountain'. In Hindu mythology, Parvati is the consort of Shiva, the god of destruction. The name symbolizes strength, stability, and endurance, much like a mountain that stands firm against the elements. Parvati embodies the divine feminine, nurturing and protecting the universe.

historical_references.reference: Parvati was a Hindu goddess and the wife of Shiva. The name Parvati is derived from the Sanskrit word Parvata which means 'mountain'.
historical_references.time_period: Clearly, the exact time period for the origin of Parvati is uncertain and can be traced back to ancient Hindu texts and mythology. However, references to Parvati can be found in the earliest known Hindu scriptures, the Vedas, which date back to around 1500 BCE.

historical_references.reference: The name Parvati is also associated with a mountain in the Western Ghats range in India, known as Parvatam Mala. This mountain has historical significance as it was believed to be the site of an ancient Hindu temple dedicated to Parvati. The temple is mentioned in various Hindu texts and inscriptions, dating back to the 2nd century BCE.
